rationale: System documentation is the control the commit plane reads better than the runtime source does, and it is the shape of the argument for most of the SA family: administrator and user documentation describing secure configuration, installation, operation and effective use is a set of documents, and a repository is a document store under version control with a content hash per commit. rampscan can evidence that the documents the repository declares exist at their declared paths, that they are non-empty, and what each one hashes to — the existence and integrity half of the control, anchored the same way every other claim here is anchored, so an edit kills the evidence with the killing commit named rather than letting the claim age quietly. This record originally claimed currency and reviewer identity on top of that — when each document last changed, which commit changed it, who reviewed that change — and it does not have them: nothing in the collector set reads git history metadata, and reviewer identity is the hosting platform's state rather than a commit's, which under a squash merge is not recoverable from the tree at all. That is the same cut the batch-1 audit made on AC-01 and RA-05 (11), applied here by the same reading when the recipe was written; the limb is named as an absence rather than borrowed from the fact that git records dates somewhere.

remainder.control: Distribution and — until a history collector exists — currency. The control requires the documentation to reach defined personnel or roles, and no commit records that anyone received or read it; that is the same gap upstream names for every policy control, and it is not closed by the document being public. Adequacy sits beside it: no assertion reads the document, so that the administrator guide actually describes secure configuration, installation and operation is a 3PAO's reading, and the declaration of what a file IS is the repository's own claim.
remainder.boundary: And the repository set. This scan read one checkout; whether it holds all the system documentation inside the authorization boundary — or the administrator guide lives in a second repository nobody pointed rampscan at — is named by a human, not by any commit. An evidenced result here means the documents named at these paths are present and unchanged since they were attested, never that the documentation set is complete.

externalSystem: Nothing. Collectors take no network by decision, execution is local, and signing is node:crypto. The documentation is read from the checkout in place; no document is uploaded to a service to be indexed, which is the usual route by which a documentation control quietly acquires an external system.
